seo.title: Homeless help in Leeds - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in Leeds: emergency housing, outreach, food, health care, benefits, work and specialist support.

page.heading: Leeds homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, serious illness, police, fire or ambulance: 999 or 112 Nowhere safe tonight or homeless: Leeds Housing Options 0113 222 4412; outside office hours 0113 378 8366 Sleeping outside or concerned about someone who is: Leeds Street Outreach 0113 245 9445 Urgent but not life-threatening medical or mental-health help: NHS 111; select option 2 for urgent mental-health support
page.notice: Beds, meals, opening times and eligibility can change. Call before travelling when possible. An assessment, application, referral or outreach contact does not guarantee accommodation or another service. Never pay anyone who claims they can secure a council or charity place.
page.intro:
Tell the worker where you are tonight, where you usually sleep, your age, whether children are with you, and whether pregnancy, disability, illness, domestic abuse, immigration restrictions or a pet affects what is safe. If a service cannot help, ask for the next safe option and write down the advice.
Start here: if you have nowhere safe tonight, call Housing Options and say clearly that you are homeless today. If you may lose your home within 56 days, ask for prevention help now. The published assessment wait can be up to four weeks for non-emergencies, so explain any same-day risk clearly.
page.footer: No Home Help does not provide emergency services or guarantee accommodation. Use nohomehelp.com. — https://nohomehelp.com/

entries.title: Emergency services
entries.description:
Phone: 999 or 112.
Call for immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, fire or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first. If you cannot speak on a mobile call to police, listen and press 55 when prompted.
NHS guidance on calling 999

entries.title: Leeds Housing Options
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 222 4412. Outside office hours call 0113 378 8366. Email: housing.options@leeds.gov.uk. — mailto:housing.options@leeds.gov.uk
Open Monday 9am–4pm, Tuesday 10am–4pm and Wednesday–Friday 9am–4pm. Call or attend if you have nowhere tonight. Email if homelessness is likely within 56 days; replies are normally within three working days. Ask to make a homeless application and explain all risks. Emergency or temporary accommodation depends on an assessment.
Housing Options contact and access
entries.address: Address: Merrion House, 110 Merrion Centre, Leeds LS2 8BB

entries.title: Leeds Street Outreach Service
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 245 9445; email: leeds.sos@cgl.org.uk. Office hours are Monday–Friday 8:30am–4:30pm, with outreach on weekdays and evenings. — mailto:leeds.sos@cgl.org.uk
Give an exact public sleeping location, usual time and description. The team can assess someone sleeping outside and connect them with emergency accommodation and other services. Contact does not guarantee that the person will be found or housed that day.
Leeds Street Outreach
entries.address: Office: 3rd Floor, Duncan House, 14 Duncan Street, Leeds LS1 6DL

entries.title: StreetLink
entries.description:
Send an alert about an adult sleeping outside when the location and time are known. StreetLink passes the information to the Leeds outreach team; it is not an emergency service or a bed-booking service. Call 999 for urgent medical danger or a child under 18 who is at risk.
Send a StreetLink alert | council rough-sleeping guidance — https://thestreetlink.org.uk/

entries.title: Simon on the Streets
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 345 2270; email: admin@simononthestreets.co.uk. — mailto:admin@simononthestreets.co.uk
Independent outreach and emotional and practical support for people who may not be engaging with other services. It does not provide emergency accommodation. Use Housing Options or Street Outreach for a same-day housing need.
Support in Leeds

entries.title: Unsafe home or domestic abuse
entries.description:
Call 999 in immediate danger. For emergency housing call Housing Options on 0113 222 4412, or 0113 378 8366 outside hours. Do not return for papers or belongings if it is unsafe.
Leeds Domestic Violence Service: 0113 246 0401, 24 hours. Accommodation is subject to assessment and availability.
Leeds domestic-violence support

categories.title: Day centres, shelter pathways and housing support

entries.title: St George's Crypt Care Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 245 9061; email: admin@stgeorgescrypt.org.uk. — mailto:admin@stgeorgescrypt.org.uk
The Care Centre offers meals, showers, clothing and support. Its emergency accommodation is accessed by referral through Leeds Housing Options on 0113 222 4412; it is not a guaranteed walk-in bed.
Care Centre | current accommodation listing — https://www.stgeorgescrypt.org.uk/how-we-help/care-centre
entries.address: Address: Great George Street, Leeds LS1 3BR

entries.title: St Anne's Resource Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 243 1894; email: starc@st-annes.org.uk. Open Monday–Friday 8:30am–4:30pm. — mailto:starc@st-annes.org.uk
For adults aged 18+ who are homeless or vulnerably housed. Services include showers, laundry, a safe mail address, housing and benefits support, referrals, and free employment, training, life-skills and English-language classes. Ask what is available that day.
St Anne's current service listing
entries.address: Address: 66 York Street, Leeds LS9 8AA

entries.title: Street Support Leeds directory
entries.description:
Search by need and location for current accommodation advice, meals, health care, practical help and specialist services. Details can change, so confirm with the provider before a long journey.
Search Street Support Leeds

entries.title: Homeless England directory
entries.description:
Search accommodation, day centres and specialist services by location and eligibility. Confirm the referral route, vacancies, age limits and pet rules directly.
Search Homeless England

entries.title: St George's Crypt weekday lunch
entries.description:
A free three-course lunch is served Monday–Friday, normally 12 noon–12:35pm. Call 0113 245 9061 before a long journey because capacity and times can change.
Leeds Food Aid Network drop-ins
entries.address: Address: Great George Street, Leeds LS1 3BR

entries.title: St Anne's breakfast and evening food
entries.description:
Breakfast starts at 8:30am Monday–Friday. Community groups normally provide evening food on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. Finish times and providers vary, so call 0113 243 1894 or check the live list before travelling.
Current Leeds food drop-ins
entries.address: Address: 66 York Street, Leeds LS9 8AA

entries.title: FoodCycle Leeds Seacroft
entries.description:
A free community meal is normally served Tuesday at 6:30pm. No booking is normally required. Meals and capacity depend on volunteers and supplies.
Food drop-in details
entries.address: Address: Chapel FM Arts Centre, York Road, Leeds LS14 6JB

entries.title: FoodCycle Leeds Beeston and Holbeck

A free community meal is normally served Wednesday at 6:30pm, without advance booking. Confirm the session on the current list.
Food drop-in details
entries.address: Address: St Luke's Church, Malvern Road, Holbeck, Leeds LS11 8PD

entries.title: UCKG Help Centre
entries.description:
Food and befriending support is normally available Saturday 11am–1pm. This is a faith-community service; check the live list before travelling.
Leeds Food Aid Network listing
entries.address: Address: 12 Regent Street, Leeds LS2 7QA

entries.title: St Aidan's food parcel
entries.description:
A food parcel session is normally held Saturday 10:30am–12 noon, without referral, with one parcel per household. Stock and rules can change.
Current food drop-ins
entries.address: Address: St Aidan's Church, Elford Place West, Leeds LS8 5QD

entries.title: Meeting Point: refugees and asylum seekers
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 279 6700. Monday sessions normally run 2:15pm–5pm with a hot meal, drinks, food parcels, low-cost clothing and household items, advocacy and digital access.
Meeting Point
entries.address: Address: Christ Church, Armley Ridge Road, Leeds LS12 3LE

entries.title: Leeds Grand Mosque halal foodbank
entries.description:
A free weekly parcel is normally available Sunday 10am–12 noon in the mosque basement. The first visit requires evidence of income or benefits and identity or address, which can make this service unsuitable if documents are missing. Email contact@leedsgrandmosque.com before attending if unsure. — mailto:contact@leedsgrandmosque.com
Food-parcel rules

entries.title: Find emergency food across Leeds
entries.description:
The Leeds Food Aid Network map includes meals, food parcels, pantries and referral routes. Some services accept direct attendance; others need a voucher or evidence. Check each entry before travelling.
Find emergency food

entries.title: St Anne's Resource Centre
entries.description:
Adults who are homeless or vulnerably housed can ask about showers, laundry, clothing and other practical support Monday–Friday 8:30am–4:30pm. Call 0113 243 1894 to check access.
St Anne's facilities
entries.address: Address: 66 York Street, Leeds LS9 8AA

entries.title: St George's Crypt
entries.description:
Ask the Care Centre about showers, clothing and practical support. Availability can depend on demand. Call 0113 245 9061.
Care Centre help
entries.address: Address: Great George Street, Leeds LS1 3BR

entries.title: Focus4Hope street support
entries.description:
Fortnightly city-centre outreach can include hot food and drinks, hygiene and underwear packs, coats, sleeping bags and footwear. Dates and locations change; check the official events list or ask St Anne's before travelling.
Focus4Hope homeless feeds

entries.title: NHS urgent care
entries.description:
Emergency: 999. Urgent but not life-threatening: 111 or NHS 111 online. Say if you have no fixed address, phone, transport or safe place to recover.
NHS 111 online

entries.title: York Street Health Practice
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 295 4840. Specialist primary care for people who are homeless or unstably housed, refugees and asylum seekers, and people using substance services.
Current NHS hours are Monday 8am–6pm, Tuesday 8am–1pm and 3pm–6pm, and Wednesday–Friday 8am–6pm; the front door opens at 8:30am. Call first, especially around Tuesday's midday closure.
NHS service details
entries.address: Address: 68 York Street, Leeds LS9 8AA

entries.title: Register with a GP without documents
entries.description:
GP care is free. You do not need proof of address, immigration status, identification or an NHS number to register. If the form asks for an address, use a temporary address or ask whether the surgery address can be used.
If refused for lack of papers, ask for the refusal in writing and contact NHS England or Citizens Advice.
NHS GP registration rules

entries.title: Urgent dental care
entries.description:
Call NHS 111 for urgent dental pain, swelling, bleeding or trauma. For routine care, use the NHS dentist search and contact practices directly. Availability and NHS acceptance change frequently.
Find an NHS dentist

entries.title: Urgent mental-health help
entries.description:
Call NHS 111 and select option 2 for urgent mental-health support. Call 999 if life is in immediate danger. Samaritans: 116 123, free at any time.
Text BRIGHT to 85258 for free, confidential, anonymous text support at any time; it is not an emergency service. — sms:85258
Leeds crisis-support options

entries.title: Dial House
entries.description:
First-time visitors can normally turn up from 6pm. Returning visitors should call 0113 260 9328 or text 07922 249452 after 6pm. Open Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 6pm–2am. — sms:+447922249452
Dial House provides a non-medical safe space for people in crisis. It is not overnight accommodation.
Dial House access information

entries.title: Here For You
entries.description:
Face-to-face emotional and practical support for people aged 16+ is normally available daily 3pm–9pm. Call or text 07760 173476 to check access. It is not a bed or emergency medical service.
Here For You details

entries.title: Forward Leeds: alcohol and drugs
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 887 2477; email: info@forwardleeds.co.uk. — mailto:info@forwardleeds.co.uk
Free, confidential advice and treatment for alcohol and drug problems. Call or use the self-referral route. Say if homelessness, withdrawal risk or medication affects safety.
74 Kirkgate service details
entries.address: City-centre hub: 74 Kirkgate, Leeds LS2 7DJ

categories.title: Toilets, internet, charging and warm spaces

entries.title: Leeds Central Library
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 378 5005. Open Monday–Wednesday 9am–8pm, Thursday–Friday 9am–5pm and Saturday 10am–4pm; closed Sunday.
Free Wi-Fi, internet computers, accessible public toilets, printing and photocopying. It is free to enter and stay. Library membership is free for people who live, work or study in Leeds, and identification is not required to join.
Central Library facilities | joining information — https://libraries.leeds.gov.uk/about-us/welcome-leeds-libraries
entries.address: Address: Municipal Buildings, Calverley Street, Leeds LS1 3AB

entries.title: Public toilets
entries.description:
Use the council's live map for locations and accessibility. The page states general opening of 10am–6:30pm but also says locking begins at 4pm, so arrive early and check the map. Some accessible toilets need a RADAR key, available for £2 from community hubs.
Leeds public-toilet map

entries.title: Community hubs
entries.description:
Hubs provide free computers and help with council services, benefits, debt, jobs and online tasks. City Centre Community Hub is at Merrion House, Woodhouse Lane, Leeds LS2 8LX; open Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday 9am–5pm and Tuesday 10am–5pm.
City Centre Community Hub | find another hub — https://www.leeds.gov.uk/community-hubs

entries.title: Welcome Spaces
entries.description:
Libraries, community hubs and partner venues provide free, safe and warm places during the colder months. Locations and seasonal hours change; use the council list before travelling.
Find a Welcome Space

entries.title: West Yorkshire Metro
entries.description:
MetroLine: 0113 245 7676, Monday–Saturday 7am–8pm and Sunday and bank holidays 8am–8pm. Ask about routes, times, fares, accessibility and live disruption.
Metro contact details

entries.title: Leeds Bus Station Travel Centre
entries.description:
Ask about journey planning and ticket options. Opening times vary, so call MetroLine before travelling. No free-travel entitlement is assumed.
West Yorkshire travel centres
entries.address: Address: York Street, Leeds LS2 7HU

entries.title: Travel for interviews or essential appointments
entries.description:
Ask a Jobshop, Jobcentre work coach, housing worker or health service before buying a ticket whether authorised travel help is available. Leeds Jobshops may help with interview travel, but approval is not automatic.
Leeds Jobshops

entries.title: Leeds Bradford Airport
entries.description:
Frequent direct buses connect Leeds and the airport. Leeds is the nearest mainline railway station, with bus connections including the A1. Check the current route, first and last bus and fare before travelling; the airport is not a shelter.
Metro airport travel information

entries.title: Leeds Crisis Payment Scheme
entries.description:
The council scheme may help with food or fuel, essential appliances, furniture or carpets, and some removal costs when fleeing violence. Apply online. If you cannot use the form, call 0800 953 2303 or 0113 376 0330, weekdays 9am–4pm, Wednesday from 10am.
A decision is normally aimed for within four working days. Evidence, a bank statement and National Insurance number may be requested. Help is assessed and is not guaranteed immediate cash.
Crisis Payment Scheme

entries.title: Universal Credit without a fixed address
entries.description:
You can claim while rough sleeping, sofa surfing or staying in a hostel. With permission, use a trusted person's, hostel, day-centre or Jobcentre address. If you lack identification, a bank account, phone, email or National Insurance number, say so: alternatives may be possible.
Tell your work coach about homelessness, mental ill health or recovery needs and ask whether the claimant commitment should change temporarily. In some supported or temporary accommodation, Housing Benefit may cover rent separately.
Universal Credit guidance for homeless people

entries.title: Leeds Welfare Rights
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 376 0452, Monday–Thursday 9am–4:30pm, Wednesday from 10:15am, and Friday 9am–4pm. Email: welfare.rights@leeds.gov.uk. — mailto:welfare.rights@leeds.gov.uk
Free benefit checks, claims, form filling, challenges and appeals. Deaf or hard-of-hearing people can text 07860 034964 to request an appointment. — sms:+447860034964
Welfare Rights

entries.title: Leeds Citizens Advice and Law Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0808 278 7878, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. A Wednesday drop-in is normally open 9am–1pm, but check before attending.
Free advice on benefits, debt, housing, employment and other problems. Take letters or notices if available, but ask for help even when documents are missing.
Citizens Advice Leeds | current contact details — https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/about-us/contact-us/local-citizens-advice/0014K000009EMKBQA4/
entries.address: Address: Oxford House, Oxford Row, Leeds LS1 3BE

categories.title: Work, training and travel to an interview

entries.title: Leeds Jobshops
entries.description:
Free drop-in help with jobs, apprenticeships, training, CVs, applications, interviews and careers. Staff may be able to help with travel to interviews. Open Monday–Friday 9am–5pm, Tuesday from 10am, without appointment. Free Wi-Fi is available.
Email: jobshops@leeds.gov.uk. Ask before buying travel because support is not automatic. — mailto:jobshops@leeds.gov.uk
Jobshop locations and help

entries.title: St Anne's classes and Big Issue North
entries.description:
Ask about free employment, training, life-skills and English-language classes. Big Issue North can explain magazine selling as a legitimate income option and offer practical support; call 0113 243 9027 or ask at St Anne's.
St Anne's services
entries.address: Address: 66 York Street, Leeds LS9 8AA

entries.title: Find vacancies and a Jobcentre
entries.description:
Use the official Find a Job service and postcode search for a current Jobcentre. A Jobcentre can help with Universal Credit, work-coach appointments and National Insurance questions.
Find a Job | find a Jobcentre — https://find-your-nearest-jobcentre.dwp.gov.uk/

entries.title: National Careers Service
entries.description:
Free advice on CVs, interviews, qualifications, training and careers for adults in England. Ask for phone or online support if travel is difficult.
National Careers Service

entries.title: RETAS: refugees and asylum seekers
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 380 5630; email: info@retasleeds.org.uk. Education, requalification, training, employment and integration support. — mailto:info@retasleeds.org.uk
RETAS Leeds
entries.address: Address: 233–237 Roundhay Road, Leeds LS8 4HS

categories.title: Housing law, debt and legal advice

entries.title: Leeds Citizens Advice and Law Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0808 278 7878, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Free advice on benefits, debt, housing, employment and some immigration issues.
Do not miss a deadline or court hearing while waiting for advice. Take notices and court papers if you have them.
Citizens Advice Leeds
entries.address: Address: Oxford House, Oxford Row, Leeds LS1 3BE

entries.title: Better Leeds Communities housing advice
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 275 4142; email: advice@betterleeds.org.uk. — mailto:advice@betterleeds.org.uk
Free, confidential advice on homelessness, possession, tenancy rights, repairs and housing problems. Appointments are required.
Housing advice

entries.title: Problems with a private landlord
entries.description:
For eviction or landlord harassment call Housing Options on 0113 222 4412 or email housing.options@leeds.gov.uk. For unsafe conditions or repairs call 0113 378 4699 or email prs.housing@leeds.gov.uk. — mailto:housing.options@leeds.gov.uk — mailto:prs.housing@leeds.gov.uk
Council help for private tenants

entries.title: Shelter emergency housing advice
entries.description:
Phone: 0808 800 4444. Check the official page for current opening hours. Shelter gives expert housing advice but cannot provide accommodation or intervene instantly in every case.
Shelter England

entries.title: Civil Legal Advice and possession court
entries.description:
Phone: 0345 345 4345, Monday–Friday 9am–8pm and Saturday 9am–12:30pm. Legal Aid advice may be available for eligible housing, debt, discrimination and domestic-abuse problems; interpreter and callback options are available.
If facing possession, attend the hearing and ask court staff for the free Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service. Do not wait for another appointment and miss court.
Civil Legal Advice | possession advice and court duty — https://www.gov.uk/guidance/legal-aid-for-possession-proceedings

entries.title: Safe mail at St Anne's
entries.description:
St Anne's Resource Centre may provide a safe correspondence address for adults who are homeless or vulnerably housed. Ask first about permission, the exact format, collection times and how long mail is kept.
Do not send post or leave identification, papers or belongings at any service without explicit permission.
St Anne's Resource Centre

entries.title: National Insurance number
entries.description:
Check old payslips, benefit letters, a tax account or UKVI account first. You may start work before receiving a number if you can prove the right to work, and do not need one to start a benefit claim.
Apply for or find a number

entries.title: Prove the right to work
entries.description:
British and Irish citizens may use an eligible passport or a birth or adoption certificate together with an official document showing the National Insurance number. Other people may use a share code or eligible immigration documents.
Do not pay an unofficial agent. Ask Citizens Advice or a regulated adviser if status is unclear.
Official right-to-work service

entries.title: Replace a birth certificate or get passport advice
entries.description:
Order certificates through the General Register Office or relevant register office; fees apply. Contact HM Passport Office before paying if documents, referees or delivery are difficult. A charity may help with an application but cannot guarantee the fee.
Order a certificate | Passport Adviceline — https://www.gov.uk/passport-advice-line

entries.title: Internet, printing and storage
entries.description:
Leeds Central Library and community hubs provide free internet access; printing may cost. No verified open-access public luggage-storage service was found. Ask a housing or day-centre worker about safe options before leaving anything.
Central Library | community hubs — https://www.leeds.gov.uk/community-hubs

entries.title: PAFRAS
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 262 2163; email: info@pafras.org.uk. Office hours are Monday–Friday 9am–4pm. PAFRAS is regulated to provide immigration advice. — mailto:info@pafras.org.uk
The admin office is not necessarily a walk-in. A Wednesday drop-in is normally held at St Aidan's Community Hall, Elford Place West, LS8 5QD, with emergency food, casework and mental-health support. Confirm and arrive early because capacity is limited.
PAFRAS contact and access
entries.address: Office: Unit 24, UNITY Business Centre, 26 Roundhay Road, Leeds LS7 1AB

entries.title: RETAS
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 380 5630; email: info@retasleeds.org.uk. Support with education, qualifications, training, employment, integration and wellbeing for refugees and asylum seekers. — mailto:info@retasleeds.org.uk
RETAS Leeds
entries.address: Address: 233–237 Roundhay Road, Leeds LS8 4HS

entries.title: Meeting Point
entries.description:
Monday sessions normally run 2:15pm–5pm for refugees and asylum seekers, with a hot meal, food parcels, low-cost essentials, advocacy and digital access. Call 0113 279 6700.
Meeting Point
entries.address: Address: Christ Church, Armley Ridge Road, Leeds LS12 3LE

entries.title: Migrant Help asylum helpline
entries.description:
Freephone: 0808 8010 503. Help with asylum support, destitution, accommodation problems and finding legal representation. Migrant Help is not a law firm.
GOV.UK asylum helplines

entries.title: Newly recognised refugees
entries.description:
Contact Housing Options immediately if asylum accommodation or support will end. Take the Home Office decision, eviction or move-on notice if available, but ask for help even when papers are missing.
Council help for new refugees

entries.title: Modern Slavery and Exploitation Helpline
entries.description:
Call 08000 121 700 for confidential guidance if someone is controlled, threatened, forced to work or have sex, has pay or documents withheld, or cannot leave. Call 999 for immediate danger.
Modern Slavery Helpline

entries.title: Leeds Domestic Violence Service
entries.description:
24-hour phone: 0113 246 0401; email: hello@ldvs.uk. — mailto:hello@ldvs.uk
Support for people of all genders, families and children, including drop-ins, specialist advocacy, safety, housing and welfare help. Emergency accommodation and refuge are subject to assessment and availability; a women-only refuge is available. Ask for an interpreter if needed.
Leeds Domestic Violence Service

entries.title: National domestic-abuse helplines
entries.description:
Women: 0808 2000 247, 24 hours. Men: 0808 801 0327. LGBT+ people: Galop 0800 999 5428. Call 999 for immediate danger.
Council domestic-abuse information

entries.title: Housing help for young people
entries.description:
Housing Options has specific help for people aged 16–21. State your age immediately. If under 18, call Children's Services on 0113 376 0336, or 0113 535 0600 outside hours. Call 999 if in danger.
People aged 16–25 can also call Centrepoint on 0808 800 0661, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm, for advice. Sofa surfing still counts as homelessness.
Centrepoint helpline | council homelessness help — https://centrepoint.org.uk/do-you-need-help/i-need-help-now/speak-someone

entries.title: Care leavers
entries.description:
Care Leaver Service: 0113 378 6771; email: dutycareleavers@leeds.gov.uk. Outside hours call 0113 535 0600. — mailto:dutycareleavers@leeds.gov.uk
Contact your personal adviser and Housing Options. Tell both services you are a care leaver and whether accommodation will end today.
Leeds leaving-care offer

entries.title: Yorkshire MESMAC
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 244 4209; email: leeds@mesmac.co.uk. Open Monday 9am–5pm, Tuesday 9am–8pm and Wednesday–Friday 9am–5pm. — mailto:leeds@mesmac.co.uk
LGBTQ+ health and wellbeing, sexual health, counselling, groups and trans support. It is not emergency accommodation.
MESMAC Leeds
entries.address: Address: 3 Park Court, 40 Park Cross Street, Leeds LS1 2QH

entries.title: Basis Yorkshire: women in sex work
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 243 0036, Monday–Friday 9:30am–4:30pm. The drop-in normally runs Monday–Wednesday 1pm–3pm, with street outreach Monday and Wednesday 8pm–10:30pm and Friday 8pm–11pm.
For women, including trans women, who live or work in Leeds and are involved in sex work. Health, safety, housing, welfare, domestic- and sexual-violence, and work or exit support.
Basis street-sex-worker support
entries.address: Address: 94 North Street, Leeds LS2 7PN

entries.title: Veterans: Op FORTITUDE
entries.description:
Phone: 0800 952 0774. Any veteran who is homeless or at risk can self-refer for housing and tenancy support through the national pathway. Accommodation is individually assessed.
The Leeds Veterans and Families Hub can also connect people with local housing, health, employment and financial support.
Veteran homelessness support | Leeds armed-forces support — https://www.leeds.gov.uk/plans-and-strategies/armed-forces-support

entries.title: Age UK Leeds
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 389 3000, Monday–Friday 10am–3pm. Free information and advice for older people on benefits, housing, health, care and local support.
Age UK Leeds contact
entries.address: Address: Bradbury Building, Mark Lane, Leeds LS2 8JA

entries.title: Adult social care and safeguarding
entries.description:
Phone: 0113 222 4401, weekdays 9am–5pm, Wednesday from 10am. Outside hours call 0113 378 0644. Email: leedsadults@leeds.gov.uk. — mailto:leedsadults@leeds.gov.uk
Ask for a care assessment or report abuse, neglect or self-neglect affecting an adult. Reports can be anonymous. Social care does not replace a homeless application; contact both services if care needs affect safe accommodation.
Adult-care referrals and safeguarding

entries.title: Street Paws
entries.description:
Street Paws works in Leeds and Yorkshire, offering veterinary support through referral and helping services consider pet-friendly options. Ask a housing or support worker about referral. Street Paws cannot directly arrange accommodation, fostering or kennels.
Email: info@streetpaws.org.uk. — mailto:info@streetpaws.org.uk
Street Paws help

entries.title: StreetVet
entries.description:
People experiencing homelessness can use the UK help form to ask about volunteer veterinary support. Eligibility and local coverage are assessed. StreetVet is not an emergency service and does not cover existing bills or provide fostering.
Request StreetVet help

entries.title: Dogs Trust Together Through Homelessness
entries.description:
The UK-wide scheme helps eligible dog owners with veterinary costs and finding dog-friendly services. A participating homelessness service may need to apply. Assessment applies; existing bills and every procedure are not automatically covered.
Together Through Homelessness

entries.title: Tell every service about your pet
entries.description:
Tell Housing Options and every referrer the species, size, health, behaviour and vaccination status. Simon on the Streets reports that one Leeds hostel has two kennels, but access and availability require referral and cannot be promised.
Do not abandon an animal or arrive at an unknown hostel expecting admission.
Simon on the Streets pet information

entries.title: Keep this page accurate
entries.description:
Services change. Please report a closed service, wrong detail or safer alternative through the project repository. Do not send private medical, immigration or housing documents.
How to contribute | report an issue — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md
